# Sensor classifier model card: sensor_v2.keras and sensor_v2_no_stage.keras

> **Simulated data.** Data: simulated; not validated on real sensors. The results below show that the training and evaluation pipeline works. They do not show that the model works on real sensors.

## Purpose
Classifies one sensor reading as normal or one of three stress classes. Fusion does not use single readings: `fusion/sensor_window.py` aggregates the labels over a 24-hour window.

## Version and files
- Version: sensor-v2
- Full model (with growth stage): sensor_v2.keras (38460 bytes), sha256 b91a3cecf2a66b75911121b05b4fea678c5a66c51f650bf189c8ba7f4e0368f7
- No-stage model (used growth stage is unknown): sensor_v2_no_stage.keras (36152 bytes), sha256 b4d8e6980dbc9c27ba639666d6ff00d8da45102da38bd1aab14e69e9b9e09bd3
- Weights are not in git. Location: MyDrive/maize-project/models/sensor/v2/
- Input: a feature vector built by `sensor/preprocessing.py` with sensor_preprocessing.json.
- Classes, in model output order: drought_stress, heat_stress, normal, waterlogging_risk.
- Decision rule: argmax, with the confidence reported.

## Data and training
Simulated rows generated by `scripts/generate_sensor_data.py` with overlap noise, in train, validation and test files (`results/sensor/generation_config.json`). Labels follow the rule baseline in `scripts/rule_baseline.py`: waterlogging above 110% of field capacity, drought below 55%, heat at 32 degrees C or above, otherwise normal (`scripts/sensor_constants.py`). The architecture and the five training seeds are as described in the implementation guide (section 2) and `scripts/train_sensor.py`; they were not re-verified here. Seed summaries: `models/mlp_sensor/seeds_summary.json`, `models/mlp_sensor/seeds_summary_no_stage.json`.

## Test results (simulated test set)
Accuracy on the test set, mean and spread over seeds, from `results/sensor/comparison.md`:

# Model Comparison

| Metric | Baseline | Full Network | No Stage Network |
|---|---|---|---|
| Accuracy | 0.9217 | 0.9490 +/- 0.0017 | 0.9500 +/- 0.0026 |
| Full - Baseline Delta | | 0.0267 | |
| No-Stage - Full Delta | | | 0.0017 |

The baseline uses the same rules that labelled the data, so a gain over it on this data says little about the gain on real sensors. The generated card `results/sensor/sensor_model_card.md` quotes 0.9483 for the full network, while the comparison table gives the mean over seeds; the reason for the difference was not checked, and this card uses the comparison table.

## Cold readings
The backend rules define normal temperature as 18 to 29 degrees C and have nothing below 18, so cold stress is not modelled. What the simulated data and the trained models do below 18 degrees C:

## Known failure modes
- Cold readings in the training data are labelled mostly waterlogging_risk, so a real cold, dry night is untested. Waterlogging at strong level maps to High severity in fusion.
- Per-reading labels carry no time structure. The simulator in `backend/simulator/run.py` changes scenario on every tick, so it never produces a sustained stress for the aggregator.

## Limitations
- Simulated data only; not validated on real sensors. The data has no time structure, so the window thresholds in fusion could not be tuned or tested on data.
- Soil moisture must be in the same units as field capacity in `scripts/sensor_constants.py` (checked against `scripts/rule_baseline.py` by `tests/test_fusion.py`).
